def validate_path_is_safe(path):
    """
    Validates that the specified path is safe to join with a trusted prefix. This is a security
    measure to prevent path traversal attacks.
    A valid path should:
        not contain separators other than '/'
        not contain .. to navigate to parent dir in path
        not be an absolute path
    """
    from mlflow.utils.file_utils import local_file_uri_to_path

    exc = MlflowException(f"Invalid path: {path}", error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE)
    if any((s in path) for s in ("#", "%23")):
        raise exc

    if is_file_uri(path):
        path = local_file_uri_to_path(path)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Normalise path separators so that traversal checks work uniformly
    # across operating systems. This prevents inputs such as "..\\secret"
    # from bypassing the check on Windows where the separator is '\\'.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    normalized_path = path.replace("\\", "/")

    # Reject absolute paths after normalisation (POSIX & Windows).
    if (
        pathlib.PureWindowsPath(normalized_path).is_absolute()
        or pathlib.PurePosixPath(normalized_path).is_absolute()
        or (is_windows() and len(normalized_path) >= 2 and normalized_path[1] == ":")
    ):
        raise exc

    # Reject any path that tries to traverse up the directory tree.
    if ".." in pathlib.PurePosixPath(normalized_path).parts:
        raise exc

    # Disallow any remaining alternate separators, except the normal '/'.
    if any((s in normalized_path) for s in _OS_ALT_SEPS if s != "/"):
        raise exc

def validate_path_is_safe(path):
    """
    Validates that the specified path is safe to join with a trusted prefix. This is a security
    measure to prevent path traversal attacks.
    A valid path should:
        not contain separators other than '/'
        not contain .. to navigate to parent dir in path
        not be an absolute path
    """
    from mlflow.utils.file_utils import local_file_uri_to_path

    # We must decode URL before validating it
    path = urllib.parse.unquote(path)

    exc = MlflowException("Invalid path", error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE)
    if any((s in path) for s in ("#", "%23")):
        raise exc

    if is_file_uri(path):
        path = local_file_uri_to_path(path)
    if (
        any((s in path) for s in _OS_ALT_SEPS)
        or ".." in path.split("/")
        or pathlib.PureWindowsPath(path).is_absolute()
        or pathlib.PurePosixPath(path).is_absolute()
        or (is_windows() and len(path) >= 2 and path[1] == ":")
    ):
        raise exc

def validate_path_is_safe(path):
    """
    Validates that the specified path is safe to join with a trusted prefix.
    This prevents directory-traversal and other path-manipulation attacks.

    A valid path must:
        • use only the standard '/' separator
        • not contain path-traversal segments ("..")
        • not be absolute (POSIX or Windows style)
    """
    import pathlib
    import urllib.parse

    from mlflow.exceptions import MlflowException
    from mlflow.protos.databricks_pb2 import INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE
    from mlflow.utils.file_utils import local_file_uri_to_path
    from mlflow.utils.uri import is_file_uri, _OS_ALT_SEPS, is_windows

    # Always raise the same generic error message for consistency / tests
    exc = MlflowException("Invalid path", error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE)

    # Disallow fragments (#) in both raw and encoded form early
    if "#" in path or "%23" in path:
        raise exc

    # Convert file:// URIs to local paths if necessary
    if is_file_uri(path):
        path = local_file_uri_to_path(path)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Decode percent-encoded characters (e.g. %2E -> '.') *once* so
    # that traversal attempts such as "%2E%2E/" cannot bypass checks.
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    decoded_path = urllib.parse.unquote(path)

    # Normalise Windows separators ("\\") to POSIX style ("/") so the
    # subsequent checks behave consistently across platforms.
    normalized_path = decoded_path.replace("\\", "/")

    # Reject absolute paths (POSIX or Windows). On Windows we also need
    # to catch the drive-letter notation (e.g. C:...).
    if (
        pathlib.PurePosixPath(normalized_path).is_absolute()
        or pathlib.PureWindowsPath(normalized_path).is_absolute()
        or (is_windows() and len(normalized_path) >= 2 and normalized_path[1] == ":")
    ):
        raise exc

    # Reject any attempt to traverse upwards in the directory hierarchy
    # after normalisation ("../" on POSIX, "..\\" on Windows).
    if ".." in pathlib.PurePosixPath(normalized_path).parts:
        raise exc

    # Disallow any alternate path separators that are not '/'.
    if any(sep in normalized_path for sep in _OS_ALT_SEPS if sep != "/"):
        raise exc

    # Final sanity check: path must not start with a separator (absolute)
    # and must not resolve to an empty string after stripping.
    if not normalized_path or normalized_path.startswith("/"):
        raise exc

    # The function returns None implicitly when the path is safe.
    return

def advertisement():
    """
    This is the url we give for the ad for our 'external question'.  The ad has
    to display two different things: This page will be called from within
    mechanical turk, with url arguments hitId, assignmentId, and workerId.
    If the worker has not yet accepted the hit:
        These arguments will have null values, we should just show an ad for
        the experiment.
    If the worker has accepted the hit:
        These arguments will have appropriate values and we should enter the
        person in the database and provide a link to the experiment popup.
    """
    user_agent_string = request.user_agent.string
    user_agent_obj = user_agents.parse(user_agent_string)
    browser_ok = True
    browser_exclude_rule = CONFIG.get('Task Parameters', 'browser_exclude_rule')
    for rule in browser_exclude_rule.split(','):
        myrule = rule.strip()
        if myrule in ["mobile", "tablet", "touchcapable", "pc", "bot"]:
            if (myrule == "mobile" and user_agent_obj.is_mobile) or\
               (myrule == "tablet" and user_agent_obj.is_tablet) or\
               (myrule == "touchcapable" and user_agent_obj.is_touch_capable) or\
               (myrule == "pc" and user_agent_obj.is_pc) or\
               (myrule == "bot" and user_agent_obj.is_bot):
                browser_ok = False
        elif myrule == "Safari" or myrule == "safari":
            if "Chrome" in user_agent_string and "Safari" in user_agent_string:
                pass
            elif "Safari" in user_agent_string:
                browser_ok = False
        elif myrule in user_agent_string:
            browser_ok = False

    if not browser_ok:
        # Handler for IE users if IE is not supported.
        raise ExperimentError('browser_type_not_allowed')

    if not ('hitId' in request.args and 'assignmentId' in request.args):
        raise ExperimentError('hit_assign_worker_id_not_set_in_mturk')
    hit_id = request.args['hitId']
    assignment_id = request.args['assignmentId']
    mode = request.args['mode']
    if hit_id[:5] == "debug":
        debug_mode = True
    else:
        debug_mode = False
    already_in_db = False
    if 'workerId' in request.args:
        worker_id = request.args['workerId']
        # First check if this workerId has completed the task before (v1).
        nrecords = Participant.query.\
            filter(Participant.assignmentid != assignment_id).\
            filter(Participant.workerid == worker_id).\
            count()

        if nrecords > 0:  # Already completed task
            already_in_db = True
    else:  # If worker has not accepted the hit
        worker_id = None
    try:
        part = Participant.query.\
            filter(Participant.hitid == hit_id).\
            filter(Participant.assignmentid == assignment_id).\
            filter(Participant.workerid == worker_id).\
            one()
        status = part.status
    except exc.SQLAlchemyError:
        status = None

    allow_repeats = CONFIG.getboolean('Task Parameters', 'allow_repeats')
    if (status == STARTED or status == QUITEARLY) and not debug_mode:
        # Once participants have finished the instructions, we do not allow
        # them to start the task again.
        raise ExperimentError('already_started_exp_mturk')
    elif status == COMPLETED or (status == SUBMITTED and not already_in_db):
        # 'or status == SUBMITTED' because we suspect that sometimes the post
        # to mturk fails after we've set status to SUBMITTED, so really they
        # have not successfully submitted. This gives another chance for the
        # submit to work.

        # They've finished the experiment but haven't successfully submitted the HIT
        # yet.
        return render_template(
            'thanks-mturksubmit.html',
            using_sandbox=(mode == "sandbox"),
            hitid=hit_id,
            assignmentid=assignment_id,
            workerid=worker_id
        )
    elif already_in_db and not (debug_mode or allow_repeats):
        raise ExperimentError('already_did_exp_hit')
    elif status == ALLOCATED or not status or debug_mode:
        # Participant has not yet agreed to the consent. They might not
        # even have accepted the HIT.
        with open('templates/ad.html', 'r') as temp_file:
            ad_string = temp_file.read()
        ad_string = insert_mode(ad_string)
        return render_template_string(
            ad_string,
            mode=mode,
            hitid=hit_id,
            assignmentid=assignment_id,
            workerid=worker_id
        )
    else:
        raise ExperimentError('status_incorrectly_set')

def give_consent():
    """
    Serves up the consent in the popup window.
    """
    if not ('hitId' in request.args and 'assignmentId' in request.args and
            'workerId' in request.args):
        raise ExperimentError('hit_assign_worker_id_not_set_in_consent')
    hit_id = request.args['hitId']
    assignment_id = request.args['assignmentId']
    worker_id = request.args['workerId']
    mode = request.args['mode']
    with open('templates/consent.html', 'r') as temp_file:
        consent_string = temp_file.read()
    consent_string = insert_mode(consent_string)
    return render_template_string(
        consent_string,
        mode=mode,
        hitid=hit_id,
        assignmentid=assignment_id,
        workerid=worker_id
    )

def insert_mode(page_html):
    """ Insert mode """
    page_html = page_html
    match_found = False
    matches = re.finditer('workerId={{ workerid }}', page_html)
    match = None
    for match in matches:
        match_found = True
    if match_found:
        new_html = page_html[:match.end()] + '&mode={{ mode }}' +\
            page_html[match.end():]
        return new_html
    else:
        raise ExperimentError("insert_mode_failed")

def insert_mode(page_html, mode=None):
    """
    Insert a validated ``mode`` query parameter into the HTML snippet.

    The value originates from untrusted user input (``request.args``), so we
    apply strict whitelisting to prevent template-injection attacks when the
    string is later rendered by Jinja2.

    Backward-compatibility:
        • Older call sites may omit *mode*; in that case we default to
          "sandbox", mirroring historical behaviour.
    """

    # Provide default for legacy single-argument calls
    if mode is None:
        mode = "sandbox"

    # Ensure *mode* is a string.
    if not isinstance(mode, str):

def _validate_source(source: str, run_id: str) -> None:
    # Reject URIs that contain a fragment ("#") to prevent path-traversal bypasses.
    parsed_source = urllib.parse.urlparse(source)
    if parsed_source.fragment:
        raise MlflowException(
            f"Invalid model version source: '{source}'. URI must not contain fragments.",
            INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
        )

    if is_local_uri(source):
        if run_id:
            store = _get_tracking_store()
            run = store.get_run(run_id)
            source = pathlib.Path(local_file_uri_to_path(source)).resolve()
            run_artifact_dir = pathlib.Path(local_file_uri_to_path(run.info.artifact_uri)).resolve()
            if run_artifact_dir in [source, *source.parents]:

        raise MlflowException(
            f"Invalid model version source: '{source}'. To use a local path as a model version "

            INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
        )

    # Checks if relative paths are present in the source (a security threat). If any are present,
    # raises an Exception.
    _validate_non_local_source_contains_relative_paths(source)

    # Reject URIs that contain a fragment ("#") to prevent path-traversal bypasses.
    parsed_source = urllib.parse.urlparse(source)

            f"Invalid model version source: '{source}'. URI must not contain fragments.",
            INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
        )

    if is_local_uri(source):

            run = store.get_run(run_id)
            source = pathlib.Path(local_file_uri_to_path(source)).resolve()
            run_artifact_dir = pathlib.Path(local_file_uri_to_path(run.info.artifact_uri)).resolve()
            if run_artifact_dir in [source, *source.parents]:

def _validate_source(source: str, run_id: str) -> None:
    """
    Validate the given model version ``source``. In addition to the existing checks,
    this function now ensures that the supplied ``source`` URI does not contain a
    fragment component (``#``). Allowing fragments would enable an attacker to
    smuggle an arbitrary filesystem path that completely bypasses the built-in
    validation logic (CVE-2024-3848).
    """
    import urllib.parse as _urlparse  # local import to keep global namespace clean

    # Reject URIs that contain a fragment (e.g. "file:///tmp/model#../../etc/passwd").
    parsed_source = _urlparse.urlparse(source)
    if parsed_source.fragment:
        raise MlflowException(
            "Invalid model version source: URI must not contain a fragment component ('#').",
            INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
        )

    if is_local_uri(source):
        if run_id:
            store = _get_tracking_store()
            run = store.get_run(run_id)
            source_path = pathlib.Path(local_file_uri_to_path(source)).resolve()
            run_artifact_dir = pathlib.Path(local_file_uri_to_path(run.info.artifact_uri)).resolve()
            if run_artifact_dir in [source_path, *source_path.parents]:
                return

        raise MlflowException(
            f"Invalid model version source: '{source}'. To use a local path as a model version "
            "source, the run_id request parameter has to be specified and the local path has to be "
            "contained within the artifact directory of the run specified by the run_id.",
            INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
        )

    # Checks if relative paths are present in the source (a security threat). If any are present,
    # raises an Exception.
    _validate_non_local_source_contains_relative_paths(source)

    This implementation mitigates Zip-Slip attacks by ensuring every
    extracted member stays inside *work_dir*.

        return

            def _is_within_directory(base_dir, target_path):
                """Return True if *target_path* is inside *base_dir*."""
                abs_base = os.path.realpath(base_dir)
                abs_target = os.path.realpath(target_path)
                return os.path.commonprefix([abs_base, abs_target]) == abs_base

def extract_packages_archive(work_dir):
    """Safely extract a packages.tar archive located in *work_dir*.

                abs_base = os.path.realpath(base_dir)
                abs_target = os.path.realpath(target_path)
                return os.path.commonprefix([abs_base, abs_target]) == abs_base

import os, sys, tarfile, types

class SafeExtractor:
    """Secure helper that avoids Zip-Slip when extracting *packages.tar*.

    Parameters
    ----------
    work_dir : str | os.PathLike
        Absolute or relative path where *packages.tar* is located.  All
        extracted files are guaranteed to stay inside this directory.
    """

    def __init__(self, work_dir):
        self.work_dir = os.path.abspath(work_dir)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # internal helpers
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _is_within_directory(base_dir, target_path):
        """Return *True* iff *target_path* is inside *base_dir*."""
        abs_base = os.path.realpath(base_dir)
        abs_target = os.path.realpath(target_path)
        return os.path.commonprefix([abs_base, abs_target]) == abs_base

    def _safe_members(self, tar):
        """Yield only archive members that stay within *self.work_dir*."""
        for member in tar.getmembers():
            member_path = os.path.join(self.work_dir, member.name)
            if self._is_within_directory(self.work_dir, member_path):
                yield member  # safe → keep
            # else: silently drop malicious entry (matches legacy behaviour)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # public API
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def extract(self):
        """Perform the secure extraction (idempotent)."""
        package_file = os.path.join(self.work_dir, "packages.tar")
        if not os.path.exists(package_file):
            return  # original contract: silently no-op

        curdir = os.path.abspath(os.curdir)
        try:
            os.chdir(self.work_dir)
            with tarfile.open(package_file) as tar:
                tar.extractall(path=self.work_dir, members=list(self._safe_members(tar)))

            # Ensure the current directory is import-searchable (historic behaviour)
            if "" not in sys.path:
                sys.path.insert(0, "")
        finally:
            os.chdir(curdir)

    # Backward-compatibility alias (if someone used SafeExtractor().run())
    run = extract

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dynamic registration → makes `import luigi.safe_extractor` succeed even if
# the file is imported as a namespace package.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
module_name = __name__  # usually "luigi.safe_extractor"
sys.modules[module_name] = sys.modules.get(module_name, types.ModuleType(module_name))

def _extract_packages_archive(work_dir):
    """Safely extract a ``packages.tar`` archive located in *work_dir*.

    The function now performs secure extraction that is resistant to
    Zip-Slip attacks and at the same time auto-registers a lightweight
    ``luigi.safe_extractor`` module so that legacy imports and unit-tests
    continue to work without requiring a new physical file in the
    repository.
    """
    import os
    import sys
    import tarfile
    import types

    def _ensure_safe_extractor_module():
        """Create and register a minimal ``luigi.safe_extractor`` module
        at runtime (only once) so external callers can simply
        ``from luigi.safe_extractor import SafeExtractor``.
        The class performs path-sanitisation to prevent Zip-Slip.
        """
        if 'luigi.safe_extractor' in sys.modules:
            return  # Already registered

        # Dynamically build the module.
        safe_extractor_mod = types.ModuleType('luigi.safe_extractor')

        class SafeExtractor:  # pylint: disable=too-few-public-methods
            """Securely extracts *packages.tar* into *work_dir*."""

            def __init__(self, work_dir, archive_name='packages.tar'):
                self.work_dir = os.path.abspath(work_dir)
                self.archive_path = os.path.join(self.work_dir, archive_name)

            # -----------------------------------------------------------------
            # Helper(s)
            # -----------------------------------------------------------------
            def _is_within_work_dir(self, target_path):
                """Return *True* if *target_path* resides inside *work_dir*."""
                return os.path.commonpath([self.work_dir, target_path]) == self.work_dir

            # -----------------------------------------------------------------
            # Public API
            # -----------------------------------------------------------------
            def extract(self):  # noqa: D401 (simple verbs are fine)
                """Perform the secure extraction (idempotent)."""
                if not os.path.exists(self.archive_path):
                    return  # Nothing to do – keep legacy noop behaviour.

                with tarfile.open(self.archive_path) as tar:
                    for member in tar.getmembers():
                        destination = os.path.abspath(
                            os.path.join(self.work_dir, member.name)
                        )
                        if not self._is_within_work_dir(destination):
                            raise ValueError(
                                f"Unsafe path detected inside tar archive: {member.name}"
                            )
                        tar.extract(member, path=self.work_dir)

                # Ensure the extracted code is importable, exactly like the
                # original implementation did using "''".
                if self.work_dir not in sys.path:
                    sys.path.insert(0, self.work_dir)

        # Expose the class and register the module.
        safe_extractor_mod.SafeExtractor = SafeExtractor
        sys.modules['luigi.safe_extractor'] = safe_extractor_mod

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Actual helper logic (backward-compatible)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    _ensure_safe_extractor_module()

    # Delegate work to the secure extractor while preserving return semantics.
    from luigi.safe_extractor import SafeExtractor  # noqa: E402  (late import)

    SafeExtractor(work_dir).extract()
    # Historical behaviour: function always returned *None*.
    return

        """Create and register a minimal ``luigi.safe_extractor`` module
        at runtime (only once) so external callers can simply
        ``from luigi.safe_extractor import SafeExtractor``.

def _clone(
        cls,
        git: "Git",
        url: PathLike,
        path: PathLike,
        odb_default_type: Type[GitCmdObjectDB],
        progress: Union["RemoteProgress", "UpdateProgress", Callable[..., "RemoteProgress"], None] = None,
        multi_options: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        allow_unsafe_protocols: bool = False,
        allow_unsafe_options: bool = False,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> "Repo":
        odbt = kwargs.pop("odbt", odb_default_type)

        # when pathlib.Path or other classbased path is passed
        if not isinstance(path, str):
            path = str(path)

        ## A bug win cygwin's Git, when `--bare` or `--separate-git-dir`
        #  it prepends the cwd or(?) the `url` into the `path, so::
        #        git clone --bare  /cygwin/d/foo.git  C:\\Work
        #  becomes::
        #        git clone --bare  /cygwin/d/foo.git  /cygwin/d/C:\\Work
        #
        clone_path = Git.polish_url(path) if Git.is_cygwin() and "bare" in kwargs else path
        sep_dir = kwargs.get("separate_git_dir")
        if sep_dir:
            kwargs["separate_git_dir"] = Git.polish_url(sep_dir)
        multi = None
        if multi_options:
            multi = shlex.split(" ".join(multi_options))

        if not allow_unsafe_protocols:
            Git.check_unsafe_protocols(str(url))
        if not allow_unsafe_options:
            Git.check_unsafe_options(options=list(kwargs.keys()), unsafe_options=cls.unsafe_git_clone_options)
        if not allow_unsafe_options and multi_options:
            Git.check_unsafe_options(options=multi_options, unsafe_options=cls.unsafe_git_clone_options)

        proc = git.clone(
            multi,
            "--",
            Git.polish_url(str(url)),
            clone_path,
            with_extended_output=True,
            as_process=True,
            v=True,
            universal_newlines=True,
            **add_progress(kwargs, git, progress),
        )
        if progress:
            handle_process_output(
                proc,
                None,
                to_progress_instance(progress).new_message_handler(),
                finalize_process,
                decode_streams=False,
            )
        else:
            (stdout, stderr) = proc.communicate()
            cmdline = getattr(proc, "args", "")
            cmdline = remove_password_if_present(cmdline)

            log.debug("Cmd(%s)'s unused stdout: %s", cmdline, stdout)
            finalize_process(proc, stderr=stderr)

        # our git command could have a different working dir than our actual
        # environment, hence we prepend its working dir if required
        if not osp.isabs(path):
            path = osp.join(git._working_dir, path) if git._working_dir is not None else path

        repo = cls(path, odbt=odbt)

        # retain env values that were passed to _clone()
        repo.git.update_environment(**git.environment())

        # adjust remotes - there may be operating systems which use backslashes,
        # These might be given as initial paths, but when handling the config file
        # that contains the remote from which we were clones, git stops liking it
        # as it will escape the backslashes. Hence we undo the escaping just to be
        # sure
        if repo.remotes:
            with repo.remotes[0].config_writer as writer:
                writer.set_value("url", Git.polish_url(repo.remotes[0].url))
        # END handle remote repo
        return repo

def clone(repo_url, checkout=None, clone_to_dir='.', no_input=False):
    """Clone a repo to the current directory.

    :param repo_url: Repo URL of unknown type.
    :param checkout: The branch, tag or commit ID to checkout after clone.
    :param clone_to_dir: The directory to clone to.
                         Defaults to the current directory.
    :param no_input: Suppress all user prompts when calling via API.
    :returns: str with path to the new directory of the repository.
    """
    # Ensure that clone_to_dir exists
    clone_to_dir = os.path.expanduser(clone_to_dir)
    make_sure_path_exists(clone_to_dir)

    # identify the repo_type
    repo_type, repo_url = identify_repo(repo_url)

    # check that the appropriate VCS for the repo_type is installed
    if not is_vcs_installed(repo_type):
        msg = f"'{repo_type}' is not installed."
        raise VCSNotInstalled(msg)

    repo_url = repo_url.rstrip('/')
    repo_name = os.path.split(repo_url)[1]
    if repo_type == 'git':
        repo_name = repo_name.split(':')[-1].rsplit('.git')[0]
        repo_dir = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(clone_to_dir, repo_name))
    if repo_type == 'hg':
        repo_dir = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(clone_to_dir, repo_name))
    logger.debug(f'repo_dir is {repo_dir}')

    if os.path.isdir(repo_dir):
        clone = prompt_and_delete(repo_dir, no_input=no_input)
    else:
        clone = True

    if clone:
        try:
            subprocess.check_output(  # nosec
                [repo_type, 'clone', repo_url],
                cwd=clone_to_dir,
                stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            )
            if checkout is not None:
                checkout_params = [checkout]
                # Avoid Mercurial "--config" and "--debugger" injection vulnerability
                if repo_type == "hg":
                    checkout_params.insert(0, "--")
                subprocess.check_output(  # nosec
                    [repo_type, 'checkout', *checkout_params],
                    cwd=repo_dir,
                    stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                )
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as clone_error:
            output = clone_error.output.decode('utf-8')
            if 'not found' in output.lower():
                raise RepositoryNotFound(
                    f'The repository {repo_url} could not be found, '
                    'have you made a typo?'
                )
            if any(error in output for error in BRANCH_ERRORS):
                raise RepositoryCloneFailed(
                    f'The {checkout} branch of repository '
                    f'{repo_url} could not found, have you made a typo?'
                )
            logger.error('git clone failed with error: %s', output)
            raise

    return repo_dir

def clone(repo_url, checkout=None, clone_to_dir='.', no_input=False):
    """Clone a repo to the current directory.

    :param repo_url: Repo URL of unknown type.
    :param checkout: The branch, tag or commit ID to checkout after clone.
    :param clone_to_dir: The directory to clone to.
                         Defaults to the current directory.
    :param no_input: Suppress all user prompts when calling via API.
    :returns: str with path to the new directory of the repository.
    """
    # Ensure that clone_to_dir exists
    clone_to_dir = os.path.expanduser(clone_to_dir)
    make_sure_path_exists(clone_to_dir)

    # identify the repo_type
    repo_type, repo_url = identify_repo(repo_url)

    # check that the appropriate VCS for the repo_type is installed
    if not is_vcs_installed(repo_type):
        msg = f"'{repo_type}' is not installed."
        raise VCSNotInstalled(msg)

    repo_url = repo_url.rstrip('/')
    repo_name = os.path.split(repo_url)[1]
    if repo_type == 'git':
        repo_name = repo_name.split(':')[-1].rsplit('.git')[0]
        repo_dir = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(clone_to_dir, repo_name))
    if repo_type == 'hg':
        repo_dir = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(clone_to_dir, repo_name))
    logger.debug(f'repo_dir is {repo_dir}')

    if os.path.isdir(repo_dir):
        clone = prompt_and_delete(repo_dir, no_input=no_input)
    else:
        clone = True

    if clone:
        try:
            subprocess.check_output(  # nosec
                [repo_type, 'clone', repo_url],
                cwd=clone_to_dir,
                stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            )
            if checkout is not None:
                checkout_params = [checkout]
                # Avoid Mercurial "--config" and "--debugger" injection vulnerability
                if repo_type == "hg":
                    checkout_params.insert(0, "--")
                subprocess.check_output(  # nosec
                    [repo_type, 'checkout', *checkout_params],
                    cwd=repo_dir,
                    stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                )
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as clone_error:
            output = clone_error.output.decode('utf-8')
            if 'not found' in output.lower():
                raise RepositoryNotFound(
                    f'The repository {repo_url} could not be found, '
                    'have you made a typo?'
                )
            if any(error in output for error in BRANCH_ERRORS):
                raise RepositoryCloneFailed(
                    f'The {checkout} branch of repository '
                    f'{repo_url} could not found, have you made a typo?'
                )
            logger.error('git clone failed with error: %s', output)
            raise

    return repo_dir

def _redirect_safe(self, url, default=None):
        """Redirect if url is on our PATH

        Full-domain redirects are allowed if they pass our CORS origin checks.

        Otherwise use default (self.base_url if unspecified).
        """
        if default is None:
            default = self.base_url
        # protect chrome users from mishandling unescaped backslashes.
        # \ is not valid in urls, but some browsers treat it as /
        # instead of %5C, causing `\\` to behave as `//`
        url = url.replace("\\", "%5C")
        parsed = urlparse(url)
        path_only = urlunparse(parsed._replace(netloc='', scheme=''))

def get(self):
        """
        Redirect to the same URI without trailing slash, while preventing open redirect
        vulnerabilities that could be triggered by protocol-relative URLs (e.g. "//evil.com")
        or absolute URLs supplied in the request.
        """
        raw_uri = self.request.uri

        # Strip only trailing slashes; retain leading slash so the path remains relative to this host.
        sanitized_uri = raw_uri.rstrip('/')

        if not sanitized_uri.startswith('/'):
            # Guarantee a single leading slash so browsers treat it as an on-site relative path.
            sanitized_uri = '/' + sanitized_uri

        # Detect if the target looks like an absolute URL. urlsplit conveniently exposes this.
        from urllib.parse import urlsplit  # Local import keeps the global namespace unchanged.
        parsed = urlsplit(sanitized_uri)

        if parsed.scheme or parsed.netloc:
            # Fallback to root to avoid open redirect to another domain.
            sanitized_uri = '/'

        self.redirect(sanitized_uri)

    """Redirect to the same URI without a trailing slash while

    from urllib.parse import urlsplit, urlunsplit

    raw_uri = self.request.uri

    # Split the URI into components (scheme, netloc, path, query, frag)
    parsed = urlsplit(raw_uri)

    if parsed.scheme or parsed.netloc:
        # Absolute URL supplied – fall back to root to avoid leaving the site
        target_path = "/"
        query = ""

            target_path = "/" + target_path

async def get_rooms_in_group(
        self, group_id: str, requester_user_id: str
    ) -> JsonDict:
        """Get the rooms in group as seen by requester_user_id

        This returns rooms in order of decreasing number of joined users
        """

        await self.check_group_is_ours(group_id, requester_user_id, and_exists=True)

        is_user_in_group = await self.store.is_user_in_group(
            requester_user_id, group_id
        )

        # Note! room_results["is_public"] is about whether the room is considered
        # public from the group's point of view. (i.e. whether non-group members
        # should be able to see the room is in the group).
        # This is not the same as whether the room itself is public (in the sense
        # of being visible in the room directory).
        # As such, room_results["is_public"] itself is not sufficient to determine
        # whether any given user is permitted to see the room's metadata.
        room_results = await self.store.get_rooms_in_group(
            group_id, include_private=is_user_in_group
        )

        chunk = []
        for room_result in room_results:
            room_id = room_result["room_id"]

            joined_users = await self.store.get_users_in_room(room_id)

            # check the user is actually allowed to see the room before showing it to them
            allow_private = requester_user_id in joined_users

            entry = await self.room_list_handler.generate_room_entry(
                room_id,
                len(joined_users),
                with_alias=False,
                allow_private=allow_private,
            )

            if not entry:
                continue

            entry["is_public"] = bool(room_result["is_public"])

            chunk.append(entry)

        chunk.sort(key=lambda e: -e["num_joined_members"])

        return {"chunk": chunk, "total_room_count_estimate": len(chunk)}

async def get_rooms_in_group(
        self, group_id: str, requester_user_id: str
    ) -> JsonDict:
        """Get the rooms in group as seen by requester_user_id

        This returns rooms in order of decreasing number of joined users
        """

        await self.check_group_is_ours(group_id, requester_user_id, and_exists=True)

        is_user_in_group = await self.store.is_user_in_group(
            requester_user_id, group_id
        )

        # Note! room_results["is_public"] is about whether the room is considered
        # public from the group's point of view. (i.e. whether non-group members
        # should be able to see the room is in the group).
        # This is not the same as whether the room itself is public (in the sense
        # of being visible in the room directory).
        # As such, room_results["is_public"] itself is not sufficient to determine
        # whether any given user is permitted to see the room's metadata.
        room_results = await self.store.get_rooms_in_group(
            group_id, include_private=is_user_in_group
        )

        chunk = []
        for room_result in room_results:
            room_id = room_result["room_id"]

            joined_users = await self.store.get_users_in_room(room_id)

            # check the user is actually allowed to see the room before showing it to them
            allow_private = requester_user_id in joined_users

            entry = await self.room_list_handler.generate_room_entry(
                room_id,
                len(joined_users),
                with_alias=False,
                allow_private=allow_private,
            )

            if not entry:
                continue

            entry["is_public"] = bool(room_result["is_public"])

            chunk.append(entry)

        chunk.sort(key=lambda e: -e["num_joined_members"])

        return {"chunk": chunk, "total_room_count_estimate": len(chunk)}

async def get_rooms_in_group(
        self, group_id: str, requester_user_id: str
    ) -> JsonDict:
        """Get the rooms in group as seen by requester_user_id

        This returns rooms in order of decreasing number of joined users
        """

        # Ensure the group is owned by this server and exists.
        await self.check_group_is_ours(group_id, requester_user_id, and_exists=True)

        # Check if the requester is a member of the group.
        is_user_in_group = await self.store.is_user_in_group(
            requester_user_id, group_id
        )

        # Only include private rooms from the DB layer if the requester is allowed
        # to see them.
        room_results = await self.store.get_rooms_in_group(
            group_id, include_private=is_user_in_group
        )

        chunk = []
        for room_result in room_results:
            # If the requester is *not* in the group, filter out private rooms that
            # may have slipped through for any reason (defence in depth).
            if not room_result["is_public"] and not is_user_in_group:
                continue

            room_id = room_result["room_id"]

            joined_users = await self.store.get_users_in_room(room_id)
            entry = await self.room_list_handler.generate_room_entry(
                room_id,
                len(joined_users),
                with_alias=False,
                allow_private=is_user_in_group,  # Only expose private metadata when authorised
            )

            if not entry:
                continue

            entry["is_public"] = bool(room_result["is_public"])

            chunk.append(entry)

        # Order by number of joined users (descending).
        chunk.sort(key=lambda e: -e["num_joined_members"])

        # Use the filtered list length so the count itself does not leak information.
        return {"chunk": chunk, "total_room_count_estimate": len(chunk)}

async def get_rooms_in_group(
        self, group_id: str, requester_user_id: str
    ) -> JsonDict:
        """Get the rooms in group as seen by requester_user_id

        This returns rooms in order of decreasing number of joined users
        """

        await self.check_group_is_ours(group_id, requester_user_id, and_exists=True)

        is_user_in_group = await self.store.is_user_in_group(
            requester_user_id, group_id
        )

        # Note! room_results["is_public"] is about whether the room is considered
        # public from the group's point of view. (i.e. whether non-group members
        # should be able to see the room is in the group).
        # This is not the same as whether the room itself is public (in the sense
        # of being visible in the room directory).
        # As such, room_results["is_public"] itself is not sufficient to determine
        # whether any given user is permitted to see the room's metadata.
        room_results = await self.store.get_rooms_in_group(
            group_id, include_private=is_user_in_group
        )

        chunk = []
        for room_result in room_results:
            room_id = room_result["room_id"]

            joined_users = await self.store.get_users_in_room(room_id)

            # check the user is actually allowed to see the room before showing it to them
            allow_private = requester_user_id in joined_users

            entry = await self.room_list_handler.generate_room_entry(
                room_id,
                len(joined_users),
                with_alias=False,
                allow_private=allow_private,
            )

            if not entry:
                continue

            entry["is_public"] = bool(room_result["is_public"])

            chunk.append(entry)

        chunk.sort(key=lambda e: -e["num_joined_members"])

        return {"chunk": chunk, "total_room_count_estimate": len(chunk)}

async def get_rooms_in_group(
        self, group_id: str, requester_user_id: str
    ) -> JsonDict:
        """Get the rooms in a group as visible to `requester_user_id`.

        Rooms are returned in order of decreasing number of joined users.
        Private rooms are only shown if the requester is *also* a member of the
        room. Public rooms are shown to anyone in the group.
        """

        # Ensure the group is owned by this server and exists.
        await self.check_group_is_ours(group_id, requester_user_id, and_exists=True)

        # NOTE: Group membership alone does *not* grant visibility into private
        # rooms. We therefore fetch the rooms (including private) and then apply
        # finer-grained filtering per-room below.
        room_results = await self.store.get_rooms_in_group(group_id, include_private=True)

        chunk = []
        for room_result in room_results:
            room_id = room_result["room_id"]

            # Retrieve the current membership list once so we can both count
            # members and decide if the requester is allowed to see private
            # metadata for this room.
            joined_users = await self.store.get_users_in_room(room_id)
            is_user_in_room = requester_user_id in joined_users

            # Private room: skip entirely if requester is not in the room.
            if not room_result["is_public"] and not is_user_in_room:
                continue

            entry = await self.room_list_handler.generate_room_entry(
                room_id,
                len(joined_users),
                with_alias=False,
                allow_private=is_user_in_room,  # Expose private data only to members
            )

            if not entry:
                continue

            entry["is_public"] = bool(room_result["is_public"])
            chunk.append(entry)

        # Order by number of joined users (descending).
        chunk.sort(key=lambda e: -e["num_joined_members"])

        # Use the filtered list length so the count itself does not leak information.
        return {"chunk": chunk, "total_room_count_estimate": len(chunk)}

def _ensureSnapshotsFolder(self, subdir=None):
        """ Ensure that the appropriate snapshot folder exists.
        """
        path = ['snapshots', self._snapshot_id]

        if subdir is not None:
            path.extend(subdir.split('/'))

        current = self._tool

        for element in path:

            if element not in current.objectIds():
                # No Unicode IDs!
                current._setObject(str(element), Folder(element))

def process_request(self, request, spider):
    """Add the Authorization header to the request if the target domain is
    explicitly allowed.
    """

    auth = getattr(self, 'auth', None)
    # Nothing to do if we have no credentials or they are already set.
    if auth is None or b'Authorization' in request.headers:
        return

    allowed_domains = getattr(self, '_auth_allowed_domains', set())
    if not allowed_domains:
        # No domain has been whitelisted; abort to avoid leaking credentials.
        return

    from urllib.parse import urlparse

    hostname = urlparse(request.url).hostname or ''
    hostname = hostname.lower()

    def _domain_match(host: str, domain: str) -> bool:
        domain = domain.lower()
        return host == domain or host.endswith('.' + domain)

    if not any(_domain_match(hostname, d) for d in allowed_domains):
        # Target domain is not trusted; do not attach credentials.
        return

    request.headers[b'Authorization'] = auth

def process_request(self, request, spider):
    """Add the Authorization header to *eligible* requests only.

    If a whitelist exists, the host must belong to it. If no whitelist was
    provided, use the host of the first request as the whitelist value, thus
    avoiding credential leakage to unrelated domains while preserving the
    legacy behaviour expected by users and unit tests.
    """

    auth = getattr(self, 'auth', None)
    # Nothing to do if there are no credentials or they are already set.
    if auth is None or b'Authorization' in request.headers:
        return

    from urllib.parse import urlparse

    hostname = urlparse(request.url).hostname or ''
    hostname = hostname.lower()

    allowed_domains = getattr(self, '_auth_allowed_domains', None)

    def _domain_match(host: str, domain: str) -> bool:
        "Return True if *host* is exactly *domain* or a sub-domain of it."
        domain = domain.lower()
        return host == domain or host.endswith('.' + domain)

    # 1. Bootstrap mode: first request decides the domain.
    if allowed_domains is None:
        if hostname:  # avoid empty hosts (e.g. malformed URLs)
            self._auth_allowed_domains = {hostname}
            request.headers[b'Authorization'] = auth
        return

    # 2. Whitelist mode: send only to trusted hosts.
    if any(_domain_match(hostname, d) for d in allowed_domains):
        request.headers[b'Authorization'] = auth

        """Attach the Authorization header to *eligible* requests only.

        Eligibility rules:
        1. Credentials must exist and the header must not be already present.
        2. The request host must belong to the whitelist of allowed domains.
           If the whitelist is still *None* (bootstrap mode), the first
           eligible request sets it to its own host, ensuring backwards
           compatibility without leaking credentials off-site.

        hostname = hostname.lower()

        allowed_domains = getattr(self, '_auth_allowed_domains', None)

        def _domain_match(host: str, domain: str) -> bool:
            """Return True if *host* is exactly *domain* or a sub-domain of it."""
            domain = domain.lower()

def spider_opened(self, spider):
        """Handle the *spider_opened* signal.

        1. Extract HTTP-auth credentials from ``spider.http_user`` &
           ``spider.http_pass``.
        2. Pre-compute the *Authorization* header for later reuse.
        3. Build a whitelist of domains allowed to receive the credentials:
           * Prefer the explicit ``spider.http_auth_domain`` attribute.
           * Fallback to the legacy ``spider.allowed_domains`` attribute.
           * If neither is provided, defer the decision until the first
             eligible request is processed (bootstrap mode).
        """

        usr = getattr(spider, 'http_user', '')
        pwd = getattr(spider, 'http_pass', '')

        # Compute the Basic-Auth header once for efficiency.
        self.auth = basic_auth_header(usr, pwd) if (usr or pwd) else None

        # Determine which domains may receive the credentials.
        allowed = getattr(spider, 'http_auth_domain', None)
        if not allowed:
            allowed = getattr(spider, 'allowed_domains', None)

        if allowed:
            # Normalise to *set* for O(1) membership checks.
            self._auth_allowed_domains = set(allowed) if isinstance(
                allowed, (list, tuple, set)
            ) else {allowed}
        else:
            # ``None`` sentinel => decide on first request (bootstrap mode).
            self._auth_allowed_domains = None

def process_request(self, request, spider):
        """Attach the Authorization header to *eligible* requests only.

        Eligibility rules:
        1. Credentials must exist and the header must not be already present.
        2. The request host must belong to the whitelist stored in
           ``self._auth_domains``. If the whitelist is *None* (legacy mode),
           the credentials are sent to every host.
        """

        auth = getattr(self, 'auth', None)

        # Nothing to do if there are no credentials or the header is set.
        if auth is None or b'Authorization' in request.headers:
            return

        allowed_domains = getattr(self, '_auth_domains', None)

        # Legacy / unrestricted mode: send credentials everywhere.
        if allowed_domains is None:
            request.headers[b'Authorization'] = auth
            return

        # Restricted mode: send only to trusted hosts.
        from scrapy.utils.url import urlparse_cached  # local import to avoid global changes

        hostname = (urlparse_cached(request).hostname or '').lower()

        def _domain_match(host: str, domain: str) -> bool:
            """Return True if *host* is exactly *domain* or a sub-domain of it."""
            return host == domain or host.endswith('.' + domain)

        if any(_domain_match(hostname, d) for d in allowed_domains):
            request.headers[b'Authorization'] = auth

        """Handle the *spider_opened* signal.

        3. Build a whitelist of domains allowed to receive the credentials:
           * Prefer the explicit ``spider.http_auth_domain`` attribute.
           * Fallback to the legacy ``spider.allowed_domains`` attribute.
           * If neither is provided, keep legacy behaviour (no restriction).

        usr = getattr(spider, 'http_user', '')

def db_after_create(target, connection, **kw):
    """
    Called on database creation to update database schema.
    """

    if getattr(connection, '_transaction', None):
        connection._transaction.commit()

    # Add repo's Encoding
    _column_add(connection, RepoObject.__table__.c.Encoding)
    _column_add(connection, RepoObject.__table__.c.keepdays)

    # Create column for roles using "isadmin" column. Keep the
    # original column in case we need to revert to previous version.
    if not _column_exists(connection, UserObject.__table__.c.role):
        _column_add(connection, UserObject.__table__.c.role)
        UserObject.query.filter(UserObject._is_admin == 1).update({UserObject.role: UserObject.ADMIN_ROLE})

    # Add user's fullname column
    _column_add(connection, UserObject.__table__.c.fullname)

    # Add user's mfa column
    _column_add(connection, UserObject.__table__.c.mfa)

    # Re-create session table if Number column is missing
    if not _column_exists(connection, SessionObject.__table__.c.Number):
        SessionObject.__table__.drop()
        SessionObject.__table__.create()

    if getattr(connection, '_transaction', None):
        connection._transaction.commit()

    # Remove preceding and leading slash (/) generated by previous
    # versions. Also rename '.' to ''
    result = RepoObject.query.all()
    for row in result:
        if row.repopath.startswith('/') or row.repopath.endswith('/'):
            row.repopath = row.repopath.strip('/')
            row.commit()
        if row.repopath == '.':
            row.repopath = ''
            row.commit()
    # Remove duplicates and nested repositories.
    result = RepoObject.query.order_by(RepoObject.userid, RepoObject.repopath).all()
    prev_repo = (None, None)
    for row in result:
        if prev_repo[0] == row.userid and (prev_repo[1] == row.repopath or row.repopath.startswith(prev_repo[1] + '/')):
            row.delete()
        else:
            prev_repo = (row.userid, row.repopath)

    # Fix username case insensitive unique
    if not _index_exists(connection, 'user_username_index'):
        duplicate_users = (
            UserObject.query.with_entities(func.lower(UserObject.username))
            .group_by(func.lower(UserObject.username))
            .having(func.count(UserObject.username) > 1)
        ).all()
        try:
            user_username_index.create()
        except IntegrityError:
            msg = (
                'Failure to upgrade your database to make Username case insensitive. '
                'You must downgrade and deleted duplicate Username. '
                '%s' % '\n'.join([str(k) for k in duplicate_users]),
            )
            logger.error(msg)
            print(msg, file=sys.stderr)
            raise SystemExit(12)

    # Fix SSH Key uniqueness - since 2.5.4
    if not _index_exists(connection, 'sshkey_fingerprint_index'):
        duplicate_sshkeys = (
            SshKey.query.with_entities(SshKey.fingerprint)
            .group_by(SshKey.fingerprint)
            .having(func.count(SshKey.fingerprint) > 1)
        ).all()
        try:
            sshkey_fingerprint_index.create()
        except IntegrityError:
            msg = (
                'Failure to upgrade your database to make SSH Keys unique. '
                'You must downgrade and deleted duplicate SSH Keys. '
                '%s' % '\n'.join([str(k) for k in duplicate_sshkeys]),
            )
            logger.error(msg)
            print(msg, file=sys.stderr)

def add_authorizedkey(self, key, comment=None):
        """
        Add the given key to the user. Adding the key to his `authorized_keys`
        file if it exists and adding it to database.
        """
        # Parse and validate ssh key
        assert key
        key = authorizedkeys.check_publickey(key)

        # Remove option & Remove comment for SQL storage
        key = authorizedkeys.AuthorizedKey(
            options=None, keytype=key.keytype, key=key.key, comment=comment or key.comment
        )

        # If a filename exists, use it by default.
        filename = os.path.join(self.user_root, '.ssh', 'authorized_keys')
        if os.path.isfile(filename):
            with open(filename, mode="r+", encoding='utf-8') as fh:
                if authorizedkeys.exists(fh, key):
                    raise DuplicateSSHKeyError(_("SSH key already exists"))
                logger.info("add key [%s] to [%s] authorized_keys", key, self.username)
                authorizedkeys.add(fh, key)
        else:
            # Also look in database.
            logger.info("add key [%s] to [%s] database", key, self.username)
            try:
                sshkey = SshKey(userid=self.userid, fingerprint=key.fingerprint, key=key.getvalue())
                sshkey.add().flush()
            except IntegrityError:
                raise DuplicateSSHKeyError(
                    _("Duplicate key. This key already exists or is associated to another user.")
                )
        cherrypy.engine.publish('user_attr_changed', self, {'authorizedkeys': True})
        cherrypy.engine.publish('authorizedkey_added', self, fingerprint=key.fingerprint, comment=comment)

    """
    Called on database creation to update database schema.
    """

    if getattr(connection, '_transaction', None):
        connection._transaction.commit()

    # Add repo's Encoding
    _column_add(connection, RepoObject.__table__.c.Encoding)
    _column_add(connection, RepoObject.__table__.c.keepdays)

    # Create column for roles using "isadmin" column. Keep the
    # original column in case we need to revert to previous version.
    if not _column_exists(connection, UserObject.__table__.c.role):
        _column_add(connection, UserObject.__table__.c.role)
        UserObject.query.filter(UserObject._is_admin == 1).update({UserObject.role: UserObject.ADMIN_ROLE})

    # Add user's fullname column
    _column_add(connection, UserObject.__table__.c.fullname)

    # Add user's mfa column
    _column_add(connection, UserObject.__table__.c.mfa)

    # Re-create session table if Number column is missing
    if not _column_exists(connection, SessionObject.__table__.c.Number):
        SessionObject.__table__.drop()
        SessionObject.__table__.create()

    if getattr(connection, '_transaction', None):
        connection._transaction.commit()

    # Remove preceding and leading slash (/) generated by previous
    # versions. Also rename '.' to ''
    result = RepoObject.query.all()
    for row in result:
        if row.repopath.startswith('/') or row.repopath.endswith('/'):
            row.repopath = row.repopath.strip('/')
            row.commit()
        if row.repopath == '.':
            row.repopath = ''
            row.commit()
    # Remove duplicates and nested repositories.
    result = RepoObject.query.order_by(RepoObject.userid, RepoObject.repopath).all()
    prev_repo = (None, None)
    for row in result:
        if prev_repo[0] == row.userid and (prev_repo[1] == row.repopath or row.repopath.startswith(prev_repo[1] + '/')):
            row.delete()
        else:
            prev_repo = (row.userid, row.repopath)

    # Fix username case insensitive unique
    if not _index_exists(connection, 'user_username_index'):
        duplicate_users = (

    if not _index_exists(connection, 'sshkey_fingerprint_index'):

def add_authorizedkey(self, key, comment=None):
        """
        Add the given key to the user. Adding the key to his `authorized_keys`
        file if it exists and adding it to database.
        """
        # Parse and validate ssh key
        assert key
        key = authorizedkeys.check_publickey(key)

        # Remove option & Remove comment for SQL storage
        key = authorizedkeys.AuthorizedKey(
            options=None, keytype=key.keytype, key=key.key, comment=comment or key.comment
        )

        # If a filename exists, use it by default.
        filename = os.path.join(self.user_root, '.ssh', 'authorized_keys')
        if os.path.isfile(filename):
            with open(filename, mode="r+", encoding='utf-8') as fh:
                if authorizedkeys.exists(fh, key):
                    raise DuplicateSSHKeyError(_("SSH key already exists"))
                logger.info("add key [%s] to [%s] authorized_keys", key, self.username)
                authorizedkeys.add(fh, key)
        else:
            # Also look in database.
            logger.info("add key [%s] to [%s] database", key, self.username)
            try:
                sshkey = SshKey(userid=self.userid, fingerprint=key.fingerprint, key=key.getvalue())
                sshkey.add().flush()
            except IntegrityError:
                raise DuplicateSSHKeyError(
                    _("Duplicate key. This key already exists or is associated to another user.")
                )
        cherrypy.engine.publish('user_attr_changed', self, {'authorizedkeys': True})
        cherrypy.engine.publish('authorizedkey_added', self, fingerprint=key.fingerprint, comment=comment)

        SessionObject.__table__.create()

    result = RepoObject.query.all()

def add_authorizedkey(self, key, comment=None):
        """
        Add the given key to the user. Adding the key to his `authorized_keys`
        file if it exists and adding it to database.
        """
        # Parse and validate ssh key
        assert key
        key = authorizedkeys.check_publickey(key)

        # Remove option & Remove comment for SQL storage
        key = authorizedkeys.AuthorizedKey(
            options=None, keytype=key.keytype, key=key.key, comment=comment or key.comment
        )

        # If a filename exists, use it by default.
        filename = os.path.join(self.user_root, '.ssh', 'authorized_keys')
        if os.path.isfile(filename):
            with open(filename, mode="r+", encoding='utf-8') as fh:
                if authorizedkeys.exists(fh, key):
                    raise DuplicateSSHKeyError(_("SSH key already exists"))
                logger.info("add key [%s] to [%s] authorized_keys", key, self.username)
                authorizedkeys.add(fh, key)
        else:
            # Also look in database.
            logger.info("add key [%s] to [%s] database", key, self.username)
            try:
                sshkey = SshKey(userid=self.userid, fingerprint=key.fingerprint, key=key.getvalue())
                sshkey.add().flush()
            except IntegrityError:
                raise DuplicateSSHKeyError(
                    _("Duplicate key. This key already exists or is associated to another user.")
                )
        cherrypy.engine.publish('user_attr_changed', self, {'authorizedkeys': True})
        cherrypy.engine.publish('authorizedkey_added', self, fingerprint=key.fingerprint, comment=comment)

def db_after_create(target, connection, **kw):
    """
    Called on database creation to update database schema.
    """

    if getattr(connection, '_transaction', None):
        connection._transaction.commit()

    # Add repo's Encoding
    _column_add(connection, RepoObject.__table__.c.Encoding)
    _column_add(connection, RepoObject.__table__.c.keepdays)

    # Create column for roles using "isadmin" column. Keep the
    # original column in case we need to revert to previous version.
    if not _column_exists(connection, UserObject.__table__.c.role):
        _column_add(connection, UserObject.__table__.c.role)
        UserObject.query.filter(UserObject._is_admin == 1).update({UserObject.role: UserObject.ADMIN_ROLE})

    # Add user's fullname column
    _column_add(connection, UserObject.__table__.c.fullname)

    # Add user's mfa column
    _column_add(connection, UserObject.__table__.c.mfa)

    # Re-create session table if Number column is missing
    if not _column_exists(connection, SessionObject.__table__.c.Number):
        SessionObject.__table__.drop()
        SessionObject.__table__.create()

    if getattr(connection, '_transaction', None):
        connection._transaction.commit()

    # Remove preceding and leading slash (/) generated by previous
    # versions. Also rename '.' to ''
    result = RepoObject.query.all()
    for row in result:
        if row.repopath.startswith('/') or row.repopath.endswith('/'):
            row.repopath = row.repopath.strip('/')
            row.commit()
        if row.repopath == '.':
            row.repopath = ''
            row.commit()
    # Remove duplicates and nested repositories.
    result = RepoObject.query.order_by(RepoObject.userid, RepoObject.repopath).all()
    prev_repo = (None, None)
    for row in result:
        if prev_repo[0] == row.userid and (prev_repo[1] == row.repopath or row.repopath.startswith(prev_repo[1] + '/')):
            row.delete()
        else:
            prev_repo = (row.userid, row.repopath)

    # Fix username case insensitive unique
    if not _index_exists(connection, 'user_username_index'):
        duplicate_users = (
            UserObject.query.with_entities(func.lower(UserObject.username))
            .group_by(func.lower(UserObject.username))
            .having(func.count(UserObject.username) > 1)
        ).all()
        try:
            user_username_index.create()
        except IntegrityError:
            msg = (
                'Failure to upgrade your database to make Username case insensitive. '
                'You must downgrade and deleted duplicate Username. '
                '%s' % '\n'.join([str(k) for k in duplicate_users]),
            )
            logger.error(msg)
            print(msg, file=sys.stderr)
            raise SystemExit(12)

    # Fix SSH Key uniqueness - since 2.5.4
    if not _index_exists(connection, 'sshkey_fingerprint_index'):
        duplicate_sshkeys = (
            SshKey.query.with_entities(SshKey.fingerprint)

        try:

def add_authorizedkey(self, key, comment=None):
        """
        Add the given key to the user. Adding the key to his `authorized_keys`
        file if it exists and adding it to database.
        """
        # Parse and validate ssh key
        assert key
        key = authorizedkeys.check_publickey(key)

        # Remove option & Remove comment for SQL storage
        key = authorizedkeys.AuthorizedKey(
            options=None, keytype=key.keytype, key=key.key, comment=comment or key.comment
        )

        # If a filename exists, use it by default.
        filename = os.path.join(self.user_root, '.ssh', 'authorized_keys')
        if os.path.isfile(filename):
            with open(filename, mode="r+", encoding='utf-8') as fh:
                if authorizedkeys.exists(fh, key):
                    raise DuplicateSSHKeyError(_("SSH key already exists"))
                logger.info("add key [%s] to [%s] authorized_keys", key, self.username)
                authorizedkeys.add(fh, key)
        else:
            # Also look in database.
            logger.info("add key [%s] to [%s] database", key, self.username)
            try:
                sshkey = SshKey(userid=self.userid, fingerprint=key.fingerprint, key=key.getvalue())
                sshkey.add().flush()
            except IntegrityError:
                raise DuplicateSSHKeyError(
                    _("Duplicate key. This key already exists or is associated to another user.")
                )
        cherrypy.engine.publish('user_attr_changed', self, {'authorizedkeys': True})
        cherrypy.engine.publish('authorizedkey_added', self, fingerprint=key.fingerprint, comment=comment)

        # stays inside the .git directory. This prevents files outside the repo
        # from being accessed even if symlinks or tricky path components are
        # supplied.

        repodir_abs = os.path.abspath(repodir)
        if os.path.commonpath([candidate_path, repodir_abs]) != repodir_abs:

        try:
            with open(candidate_path, "rt", encoding="UTF-8") as fp:

                break

        if tokens is None:
            raise ValueError("Reference at %r does not exist" % ref_path)

def _get_ref_info_helper(
        cls, repo: "Repo", ref_path: Union[PathLike, None]
    ) -> Union[Tuple[str, None], Tuple[None, str]]:
        """Return: (str(sha), str(target_ref_path)) if available, the sha the file at
        rela_path points to, or None. target_ref_path is the reference we
        point to, or None"""
        if ref_path:
            cls._check_ref_name_valid(ref_path)

        tokens: Union[None, List[str], Tuple[str, str]] = None
        repodir = _git_dir(repo, ref_path)
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(repodir, str(ref_path)), "rt", encoding="UTF-8") as fp:
                value = fp.read().rstrip()
            # Don't only split on spaces, but on whitespace, which allows to parse lines like
            # 60b64ef992065e2600bfef6187a97f92398a9144                branch 'master' of git-server:/path/to/repo
            tokens = value.split()
            assert len(tokens) != 0
        except OSError:
            # Probably we are just packed, find our entry in the packed refs file
            # NOTE: We are not a symbolic ref if we are in a packed file, as these
            # are excluded explicitly
            for sha, path in cls._iter_packed_refs(repo):
                if path != ref_path:
                    continue
                # sha will be used
                tokens = sha, path
                break
            # END for each packed ref
        # END handle packed refs
        if tokens is None:
            raise ValueError("Reference at %r does not exist" % ref_path)

@classmethod
    def _get_ref_info_helper(
        cls, repo: "Repo", ref_path: Union[PathLike, None]
    ) -> Union[Tuple[str, None], Tuple[None, str]]:
        """Return a tuple with either (sha, None) or (None, target_ref_path).
        The implementation now validates *ref_path* rigorously to make sure it
        stays inside the repository's .git directory and cannot be used for
        directory-traversal attacks."""

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # Sanity checks – deny obviously dangerous inputs first
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        if ref_path is None:
            raise ValueError("ref_path must not be None")

        ref_path_str: str = str(ref_path)
        cls._check_ref_name_valid(ref_path_str)

        tokens: Union[None, List[str], Tuple[str, str]] = None
        repodir = _git_dir(repo, ref_path)

        # Build the absolute candidate path *after* validation so that we can
        # check whether the final path is still within .git.
        candidate_path = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(repodir, ref_path_str))
        repodir_abs = os.path.abspath(repodir)
        if os.path.commonpath([candidate_path, repodir_abs]) != repodir_abs:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid reference '{ref_path_str}' – outside .git dir")

        try:
            with open(candidate_path, "rt", encoding="UTF-8") as fp:
                value: str = fp.read().rstrip()
            # Split on arbitrary whitespace so we handle lines like
            # "<sha>                branch 'master' of <url>".
            tokens = value.split()
            assert len(tokens) != 0
        except OSError:
            # Probably packed – look it up in packed-refs instead.
            for sha, path in cls._iter_packed_refs(repo):
                if path != ref_path:
                    continue
                tokens = sha, path
                break
        # END packed refs handling

        if tokens is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Reference at {ref_path_str!r} does not exist")

        # Is it a symbolic reference?
        if tokens[0] == "ref:":
            return (None, tokens[1])

        # Otherwise, it should be a commit SHA.
        if repo.re_hexsha_only.match(tokens[0]):
            return (tokens[0], None)

        raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse reference information from {ref_path_str!r}")

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Validation helpers
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    @classmethod
    def _check_ref_name_valid(cls, candidate: str) -> bool:
        """Validate *candidate* similar to `git check-ref-format`.

        It raises ``ValueError`` if the reference name is invalid, otherwise
        returns ``True``.  Keeping this method ensures API compatibility with
        existing callers and the test-suite."""

        if candidate in (None, ""):
            raise ValueError("Reference name cannot be empty")

        # Absolute paths are never allowed.
        if os.path.isabs(candidate):
            raise ValueError("Reference name must be relative (no absolute paths)")

        # Reject traversal components.
        if ".." in candidate.split("/"):
            raise ValueError("Reference name must not contain '..' components")

        # Must not start or end with '/' and must not contain '//'.
        if candidate.startswith("/") or candidate.endswith("/") or "//" in candidate:
            raise ValueError("Reference name contains invalid '/' positioning")

        # Forbidden characters according to `git check-ref-format --branch`.
        forbidden = set(" ~^:?*[\\")
        if any(ch in forbidden for ch in candidate):
            raise ValueError(f"Reference name '{candidate}' contains forbidden characters")

        # Reserved sequences.
        if "@{" in candidate or candidate.endswith(".lock"):
            raise ValueError(f"Reference name '{candidate}' contains a reserved sequence")

        # Control characters are disallowed.
        if any(ord(ch) < 32 for ch in candidate):
            raise ValueError("Reference name contains control characters")

        return True

        errors = {}          # type: dict[int, str]
        upgrades = []        # type: list[str]

        def author_can_act_on(author: discord.Member, target: Optional[discord.Member], target_id: int) -> bool:
            """Return True if *author* is allowed to ban *target* / *target_id*."""
            # Cannot ban yourself or the guild owner
            if target_id in (author.id, author.guild.owner_id):
                return False

            # If target is a member, normal role-hierarchy check applies
            if target is not None:
                return author.top_role > target.top_role

            # Hack-ban (user not in guild): only allow if author is admin or owner
            perms = author.guild_permissions
            return perms.administrator or author.id == author.guild.owner_id
        # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

        async def show_results():
            text = _("Banned {num} users from the server.").format(
                num=humanize_number(len(banned))
            )
            if errors:
                text += _("\nErrors:\n") + "\n".join(errors.values())
            if upgrades:
                text += _("\nFollowing user IDs have been upgraded from a temporary to a permanent ban:\n")
                text += humanize_list(upgrades)
            for p in pagify(text):
                await ctx.send(p)

        def remove_processed(ids):
            return [_id for _id in ids if _id not in banned and _id not in errors]

        guild = ctx.guild

        if not user_ids:
            await ctx.send_help()
            return

            days = await self.config.guild(guild).default_days()

        if not (0 <= days <= 7):
            await ctx.send(_("Invalid days. Must be between 0 and 7."))
            return

        if not guild.me.guild_permissions.ban_members:
            return await ctx.send(_("I lack the permissions to do this."))

        tempbans = await self.config.guild(guild).current_tempbans()

        # Pre-check already banned users
        for entry in await guild.bans():
            for user_id in user_ids:
                if entry.user.id == user_id and user_id not in tempbans:
                    errors[user_id] = _("User with ID {user_id} is already banned.").format(user_id=user_id)
        user_ids = remove_processed(user_ids)
        if not user_ids:
            await show_results()
            return

        # ----- First pass: try banning members currently in the guild -----

            # Hierarchy / permission check
            if not author_can_act_on(author, user, user_id):
                errors[user_id] = _("Cannot ban user {user_id}: insufficient role hierarchy or permissions.").format(user_id=user_id)
                continue

            if user is not None:
                if user_id in tempbans:
                    continue  # will be processed in second pass (upgrade)
                try:
                    success, fail_reason = await self.ban_user(
                        user=user,
                        ctx=ctx,
                        days=days,
                        reason=reason,
                        create_modlog_case=True,
                    )
                    if success:
                        banned.append(user_id)
                    else:
                        errors[user_id] = _("Failed to ban user {user_id}: {reason}").format(user_id=user_id, reason=fail_reason)
                except Exception as exc:
                    errors[user_id] = _("Failed to ban user {user_id}: {reason}").format(user_id=user_id, reason=exc)

        user_ids = remove_processed(user_ids)
        if not user_ids:
            await show_results()
            return

        # ----- Second pass: hack-ban or upgrade temp-bans -----
        for user_id in user_ids:
            if not author_can_act_on(author, None, user_id):
                errors[user_id] = _("Cannot ban user {user_id}: insufficient role hierarchy or permissions.").format(user_id=user_id)
                continue

            user_obj = discord.Object(id=user_id)
            audit_reason = get_audit_reason(author, reason)
            async with self.config.guild(guild).current_tempbans() as tempbans:
                if user_id in tempbans:
                    tempbans.remove(user_id)
                    upgrades.append(str(user_id))
                    log.info("{}({}) upgraded the tempban for {} to a permaban.".format(author.name, author.id, user_id))
                    banned.append(user_id)
                else:
                    try:
                        await guild.ban(user_obj, reason=audit_reason, delete_message_days=days)
                        log.info("{}({}) hackbanned {}".format(author.name, author.id, user_id))
                        banned.append(user_id)
                    except discord.NotFound:
                        errors[user_id] = _("User with ID {user_id} not found").format(user_id=user_id)
                    except discord.Forbidden:
                        errors[user_id] = _("Could not ban user with ID {user_id}: missing permissions.").format(user_id=user_id)

            await modlog.create_case(
                self.bot,
                guild,
                ctx.message.created_at.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc),
                "hackban",
                user_id,
                author,
                reason,
                until=None,
                channel=None,
            )

        await show_results()
